industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence moved towards the tape. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): third-quarter beats were sold (Sandvik down 5%, Atlas Copco down 8%, Hiab down 12%), Danske Bank's C-J (25 October) says 'a lot is priced in' with the order strength coming from data centres the market no longer pays for, and the exception is the non-AI compounder (Hexagon, 13% organic growth); against it, offshore services and nuclear have multi-year visibility and electrical equipment is still the physical bottleneck. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment, Diversified groups, Distributors, Test and measurement and Engineered components at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Five live holdings (19.35 points of the book) sit here, judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: a tape that sells beats is a regime statement; for B: the order data remain the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack. To D on a second week of beats sold with relative strength falling to F.

sector.why: Neutral, set deliberately this week (carried C). Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): cyclical component makers into a growth scare, against the restock evidence in the bottom-up work: DiscoverIE's memo (Mixed) records 'the sector-wide end of destocking' and proven Stage 2 momentum while its acquisition funding fights the Fragility axis; Ericsson beat on network equipment. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: B now, B prior, the market is paying. One live holding, Volex (4.42%, Technical Momentum A, TSR/Valuation F), judged in component 4; two MI Pool names, DiscoverIE and Senior. Counter-case for higher: persistent relative strength and the restock; for lower: components are the first order cut when the margin rolls over. Balanced, so Neutral by judgement.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the re-test written last week (Neutral against Underweight after the Bank of England's decision and guidance on 5-Nov-26) could not run, because no source in the pack reports the outcome; the only United Kingdom items are undated headlines (the pound firmer on policy divergence; shoppers 'more upbeat than their European counterparts', City AM, against a GfK 'weakens in November' headline most likely from 2025). Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). The Budget read of last week stands: a UK-specific fiscal tail risk removed without lowering the rate; 22 of the Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Counter-case unchanged: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance when the 5-Nov-26 decision is read, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.

items.criterion: Industry RS below 30, read each Friday

The whole holding (three tranches, 5.64% at current value) was due to sell at the Tue 10-Nov session; no sale is recorded, so the signal stands.
Fri 13-Nov reads it again, a day after the results; 30 or more needs one place, about 6.7 points.

items.criterion: Relative price more than 25% below its 52W high, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal at the 30-Oct month-end (21.6% below); 26.2% below on 10-Nov, beyond the line.
1.9% below on 9-Oct, 21.6% on 30-Oct, 28.0% on 5 and 6-Nov, 26.2% on 10-Nov.
Read Mon 30-Nov; 548.82p at a flat market (1.6% above the close) clears it.

items.criterion: SS Sales or SS PT Net Upgrade Breadth below zero AND Stock RS below 50, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal at 30-Oct (Stock RS 78); on 10-Nov PT Net Upgrade Breadth (14%) is below zero and Stock RS 50 sits on the line.
PT Net Upgrade Breadth unchanged since 21-Oct (four unnamed brokers cutting); revenue breadth +71%, from +100%, none cutting; Stock RS 46 on 6-Nov.
Read Mon 30-Nov; Stock RS at 49 completes it; net PT raising after 12-Nov removes it.

items.criterion: Sector RS below 50 with Stock RS below 70, read at the month-end

Sector RS 70 to 45 to 57 from 30-Oct to 6-Nov to 10-Nov: moving away from the line.
Read Mon 30-Nov; Sector RS needs 8 points, to 49; Stock RS back to 70 also clears it.

items.criterion: A tranche 30% below its highest close since purchase, with Stock RS below 70

bullets.text: No sell signal: tranches 1 and 2 need a close below 489.3p (9.4% down); tranche 3 below 413.0p (23.5% down).
Stock RS (50) is already below 70, so the price half alone decides.
A triggered tranche sells at the Tuesday session after its release (a 15% rebound from its low, or 63 trading days).

Not reachable on 13-Nov; about 412p on 20-Nov or 492p on 27-Nov, at a flat market.

bullets.text: Volex is 5.64% of capital at current value (5.52% at entry) against the 6.68% limit: 1.04% of room.
About 0.62 of a 1.67% tranche; the room does not override the sell signal.

adds.criterion: Where Volex stands for an add: pulling back or basing; may be retesting or forming a VCP; healthily retesting or breaking out

bullets.text: None of the three stages: the pullback has become a broken trend on your medium-term tests.

The Master Dashboard reads Pulling Back Plausible (3 of 4), Basing Possible (1 of 4), Healthy Retest Possible (3 of 6, no MA retested), no volatility contraction pattern; Volex is 3.2% below the absolute 200D MA after failing at it on 10-Nov.
A heavy-volume close above about 559p restores a retest; a close below 497p breaks the July base.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a positive retest of a rising MA

bullets.text: Absent: Volex has closed below the rising absolute 200D MA for five sessions, 3.2% below on 10-Nov.
It fell 5.9% below on 5-Nov on 3.83 times the 50D average; Tuesday's rebound reached 556p, 0.4% short, on 0.64 times, and closed near its low.
A heavy-volume up day closing above about 559p, most plausibly on the 12-Nov results.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a broadening of the case (momentum rising in guidance, sell-side estimates, technicals or peers)

bullets.text: Partly present: guidance raised on 19-Oct ("towards the upper end"); FY2027 EPS +15.0% in three months, but breadth eased to +71% on 9-Nov.
Absent on technicals (Technical Momentum D, broken trend) and peers (four of Volex's seven closest peers below their absolute 200D MAs; the chain de-rating as it upgrades).
12-Nov results with working capital falling and data-centre revenue stable, then net PT raising.
On 10-Nov you wrote: "I really like the investment case… But I struggle to find justifications to own it on the rules we have".
Your playbook adds nothing to Volex; after any exit it becomes eligible for a Speculative Bet of a 3% of AUM tranche, on tests none of which passes today.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
